gold_rationale: AAV-PRKN gene addition is the mechanistically correct modality for autosomal-recessive, biallelic loss-of-function PRKN PD: restoring parkin addresses the causal mitophagy/mitochondrial-QC defect (unlike dominant gain-of-function targets, which need lowering). Progression should be conditional on CNS delivery/coverage of nigrostriatal regions, controlling parkin overexpression, managing capsid/transgene immunity, genetically confirming the rare biallelic-PRKN population and treating early given slow progression, selecting mitochondrial/imaging biomarkers and endpoints sensitive enough for a slowly progressive rare disease, and validating in PRKN/PINK1 models despite their mild phenotypes. A clean genetic rationale is not demonstrated efficacy/safety, and the rare-population, slow-progression trial design is a major challenge.
required_concepts: gene addition correct for recessive loss-of-function
red_flags: claims proven efficacy/safety without clinical evidence
ignores capsid or transgene immune response
ignores CNS delivery / nigrostriatal coverage challenge
fails to require genetic confirmation of biallelic PRKN status / mismatches the modality to the genetics
